st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the pork and beef in batches for 10 minutes total.
Add the onion and garlic and cook 4 minutes. Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Add [[6 cups]] water and the thyme. Cover and simmer for 60 minutes until the meat is tender.
Add the squash, eggplant and whole pepper. Simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and simmer 15 minutes until everything is soft and the stew is thick. Remove the whole pepper.
For the fungee, bring [[4 cups]] water and the sliced okra to a boil with [[1.5 tsp]] salt. Cook 5 minutes until the okra is tender.
Whisk the cornmeal slowly into the pot with the okra. Cook over low heat, stirring hard with a wooden spoon, for 8 minutes until it pulls away from the pan.
Shape the fungee into balls or a mound using a wet bowl.
Serve the fungee with the pepperpot stew spooned over or alongside.
Grate the sweet potatoes finely into a large bowl.
Stir in [[1 cup]] shredded coconut, [[0.5 cup]] brown sugar, [[0.25 cup]] raisins, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[1 tsp]] vanilla and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Fold in [[0.75 cup]] flour until you have a thick, sticky mixture that holds together.
Soften banana leaves over a flame for a few seconds, or use foil or parchment squares with a little oil on them.
Put about [[0.5 cup]] of the mixture in the middle of each piece and shape it into a log.
Fold the wrapping over the log and tie or fold the ends tight so water cannot get in.
Place the bundles in a pot with 1 inch of boiling water and a lid, or in a steamer basket.
Steam for 60 minutes, adding more hot water if the pot gets low.
Rest 10 minutes, unwrap, and serve warm or cold.
Soak the salt cod in cold water for at least 8 hours or overnight in the fridge, changing the water 3 times.
Drain, put the fish in a pot with [[6 cups]] fresh water and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse. Taste a flake: if still too salty, boil again with fresh water.
Flake the fish into bite-size pieces, removing any bones or skin.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, thyme and scotch bonnet and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes until they soften.
Add the flaked fish and [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper. Cook 5 minutes, stirring gently. Do not add salt.
Serve hot with ducana, bread or boiled root vegetables.
Put the pork in a pot with water to cover, boil for 25 minutes to remove excess salt, then drain.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot. Cook the pork for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the onion, garlic and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, the thyme, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper for 1 minute.
Add the beans and the rinsed rice and stir 1 minute to coat in the seasoning.
Pour in [[4 cups]] water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover tightly, and cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat, then fluff with a fork and remove the thyme stems.
Whisk [[3 cups]] flour, [[1.5 tbsp]] baking powder, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Rub in [[3 tbsp]] cold butter with your fingers until the mix looks like coarse crumbs.
Add about [[0.75 cup]] milk a little at a time and mix until a soft dough forms.
Knead gently for 1 minute, then cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 10 balls and flatten each into a disc about 0.5 inch thick.
Heat [[1.5 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry 3 or 4 cakes at a time for 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with butter, cheese or stewed saltfish.
